text:
anna: Quick follow-up from the all-hands — thanks everyone. A few customers mentioned last-minute scope cuts. Can leadership share the strongest hypotheses for why we lost those deals so I can synthesize and pass to GTM?

raj: Short version: two main buckets — cost/unit economics and missing integration hooks for their data plane. Also one deal had security audit concerns.

maria: Agree with Raj. For the cost point, the customer was comparing our Dedicated pricing vs building a smaller self-hosted stack. They valued our SLOs but the TCO numbers looked too high on their model.

tom: On integrations — which hooks were missing? I thought we had the connector for their S3-compatible store?

maria: They needed streaming ingestion and an in-proc SDK for Java 11 (their stack is legacy). The connector existed but not with the low-latency batch path they wanted.

katie: Also saw feature ask: deterministic audit logs for inference calls (per-token provenance). That came up in compliance-heavy accounts.

ben: Noted a separate pattern: the sales cycle elongated because evals failed on long-tail prompts — quality regressions vs their baseline. Evals team, can we surface the top failing prompts?

anna: @ben good call — can you collect top 5 regression prompts per lost deal and drop in this thread?

ben: Will do. ETA EOD.

raj: Actionable asks from leadership side: 1) Product: quick scoping for lightweight streaming connector + Java SDK patch. 2) Pricing: run a competitive TCO scenario for Dedicated vs self-host over 12/24 months. 3) Security: prioritize deterministic audit log spec (paper design ok).

maria: For product prioritization — we can spin up a 2-sprint plan for the connector and SDK patch as a P0 for mid-market segment. Need eng estimate.

tom: I can allocate two engineers to prototype the low-latency path next week. Will sync with @maria for acceptance criteria.

katie: On pricing, we should also model a burstable overlay (small reserved + burst) that maps closer to their cloud model. That might close TCO gaps.

raj: Yes — compute a model where customers reserve 25% and burst 75% on demand. Finance can help with numbers.

anna: Request from comms: I want a one-paragraph summary for leadership to share with the customer success teams by tomorrow. Draft below — please edit inline.

anna (draft): "We lost three mid-market deals due to a combination of higher-than-expected TCO and missing low-latency integrations for legacy stacks. Short-term plan: prototype a streaming connector and Java SDK patch (2 sprints), produce a competitive TCO overlay (reserve+burst), and ship a deterministic audit-log spec. We will follow up with tailored evals and a cost model within 7 business days."

maria: LGTM with two edits: change "we lost three" -> "several" and add "assign owners" to timeline.

raj: Add: "sales will offer a limited pilot pricing for accounts willing to validate the burstable model."

anna: Updated draft and will send.

ops-bot: Reminder: create tickets for product/eng/pricing tasks tagged #all-hands-followup.

ben: I uploaded the initial regression prompt set to the shared drive: link (private). Will add per-deal notes.

tom: I'll start the prototype branch today and post status in eng-runtime.

katie: I'll coordinate with security to draft the audit-log spec. ETA 3 business days.

maria: Thanks everyone. If any customer managers want to add specifics, drop them here — we'll keep this as the single source for follow-ups.

anna: Closing the loop: I'll compile everything and circulate to CSMs and salessending by 11:00 PT tomorrow. :thumbsup:
